title: How to Choose the Right Networking Standard for Your IoT Device
summary: We answer what is the IoT and navigate the complex world of the various networking standards that are enabling this sensor revolution.
body_text: Whether your IoT device is two feet or two continents away from its base station, you have options. From time to time, one of the major electronics manufacturers—Samsung, LG, and Sony are among the usual suspects—will introduce a new networked appliance or gadget at an event like CES (remember when live trade shows were a thing?) that will inspire a spate of articles about how the Internet of Things revolution is just on the cusp of changing our lives forever. But the Internet of Things (IoT) is no longer just a buzzword designed to generate online excitement and grab reporters’ ink. In truth, the rollout of IoT technology has been progressing surely and steadily for years, growing momentum as it is adopted by new industries and integrated seamlessly into new facets of everyday life. Before we go further, perhaps it’s useful to take a quick step back and address the question, what is the Internet of Things? Simply put, it refers to the ever-expanding range of devices and objects that can be networked. This not only allows users to remotely manipulate these devices, but more importantly, allows sensors in the devices to collect data about its environment and send it back to a central database. This is where IoT really shows the promise to change the technological paradigm. Once this data is collected, it can be analyzed to optimize processes and contribute to machine learning algorithms that improve software performance over time. All of these benefits depend on the ability to integrate sensors and network connectivity into any product imaginable. As a world-leading trusted advisor and technology partner for human-machine interface (HMI) devices, sensors, and other cutting-edge technologies, we have plenty of standard sensors and expertise in building custom sensors. However, we are also full-service integrators, meaning we can provide engineering resources to also help our customers solve the networking side of the equation. Long gone are the days when devices were tethered to Ethernet cables; there are a plethora of wireless connectivity options available, each with its own use case depending on distance and power requirements. In this post, we’ll explore the different tiers of wireless connectivity—sorted by range—and the advantages and drawbacks offered by each. The most noteworthy and recognizable personal area network (PAN) standard is Bluetooth, which is often found in consumer electronics because it requires the master device (often the user’s phone) to be in relatively close proximity to the edge device—usually the same room. This makes it a great solution for things like heart rate-monitoring headphones, game controllers, and smart watches, among many others. The main drawback, of course, is its range. Anyone whose favorite song has unexpectedly cut out after they absentmindedly walked too far from their wireless speakers is familiar with this issue. Basic Bluetooth power consumption is fairly low, but the standard also supports Bluetooth LE, a low-power version that uses between half and one hundredth as much power—depending on the use case. This energy efficiency comes at the cost of a slower data rate, but makes the standard more useful for IoT devices that rely on battery power. While Bluetooth reigns supreme, there are other formats in the wireless PAN segment that are worth considering. For instance, Zigbee is a low-power, low-bandwidth standard that is especially useful for applications like medical devices, home automation, and other energy-sipping sensors. Like Bluetooth is for PANs, the various 802.11 protocols, commonly known as Wi-Fi, comprise the dominant standard for wireless local area networks (LANs). Wi-Fi has already been part of most of our lives for many years, and this ubiquity makes it an attractive choice for IoT networking. After all, IT staffs are already used to working with it and likely already have infrastructure in place. It has also become very secure over time because it is such a common target for attack—most vulnerabilities have already been uncovered and fixed. Compared to Bluetooth, Wi-Fi offers significantly longer range, which can be further expanded by adding repeaters to create a mesh network. This makes it a great option when coverage needs to encompass a building, factory, or small campus. Not only does it transmit farther, Wi-Fi offers the highest throughput and data rate of any technology on this list. However, these advantages come at the cost of high power usage. This makes Wi-Fi most effective for applications with access to power mains. But when you need to distribute your IoT sensors far and wide, you’ll need something a bit more specialized. The holy grail of IoT networking, these emerging standards generally transmit data at slower speeds but offer ranges that span miles instead of yards. These technologies also use less power than their alternatives, which allows sensors to keep transmitting data for years on end while powered by a small battery or energy harvested from the environment. (you can learn more in our previous post: The Energy We Need to Power the IoT Revolution Is All Around Us…If You Know Where to Look.) The tradeoff is significantly slower transfer speeds and lower throughput, which is why low-power wide area networks (LPWAN) are most effectively employed on widely distributed networks of low-power sensors that don’t need to constantly transmit data back to a base station. For example, a moisture sensor in a field of crops or an air quality monitor in a city only need to collect and transmit data at certain intervals during the day. In industrial IoT settings, sensors on certain machinery may be located in particularly inaccessible spots, which makes the extended battery life of these sensors even more appealing. Unlike the previously mentioned tiers, this space is still a Wild West of sorts, with multiple standards competing for market share. However, many do share common traits. Typically, these standards rely on radio frequency (RF) technology, which uses radio waves to transmit data packets from edge devices to base stations, which can then send the information along for analysis or storage. A number of leading protocols, including SigFox, LoRa, and Dash 7, operate in the unlicensed frequency range, while others—such as NB-IoT and EC-GSM-IoT—operate in the range licensed for cellular data. Once again, this presents a trade-off. The unlicensed bands, by virtue of their open nature, are more heavily saturated than the regulated bands, which means transfer speeds are slower. However, standards operating in the regulated frequencies need to pay licensing fees, making the service more expensive. Which standard is best for your particular application will be mostly be dependent upon your bandwidth needs. The leading wireless wide area network (WWAN) for IoT is one we are all already intimately familiar with. (You might even be using it to read this post right now.) Cellular telecommunications standards like 2G, 3G, 4G, and even the new 5G can be harnessed for IoT networking when fast data rates are required or you would rather take advantage of the existing cellular infrastructure instead of deploying an LPWAN. Of course, since you’re using a telecoms company’s cellular equipment, you will have to pay for a plan that fits your data usage forecast. These standards are also more power hungry (especially when you start using 4G or 5G), which rules them out for agricultural or industrial IoT applications in which the sensors are located in inaccessible spots, making replacing batteries an onerous chore. A less developed segment of WWAN networking options uses satellites to communicate with IoT devices. Most of these networks are still being tested or deployed, so the technology is still in its early stages. However, it is certainly a segment we will be keeping our eye on. Interlink Electronics is rooted in sensor technology, and the emergence of the IoT is the biggest thing to ever happen to the industry. Soon, sensor technology will allow the devices we use at work and home to better react to their surroundings and learn to become more efficient over time. As a full-service IoT integrator, we don’t just help your business develop the best sensor technology for your IoT product, we also work with your team to select and integrate the right networking standard for the job. If you would like to discuss your IoT project and how we can help in greater detail, please don’t hesitate to reach out today!

Bonnie Thompson COO at Forest Family Dentistry Frequently Asked Questions How much do payroll services cost? Payroll services usually include a monthly base fee plus a per-employee charge. In most cases, the base fee falls between $40–$60, with per-employee rates ranging from $4–$12. Exact costs vary by provider, since some include features like tax filing and benefits in the base price while others charge separately. Are there different types of payroll companies? Yes, payroll companies generally fall into these categories: basic payroll processors that handle calculations and tax filing, full-service providers that include HR features and benefits administration, and comprehensive platforms like Rippling that integrate payroll with other business functions. What services are included in the base price? Most base plans include payroll processing, payroll tax calculations and filing, direct deposit, employee self-service portals, and basic reporting. Advanced features like benefits administration, time tracking, and HR tools often cost extra or require higher-tier plans. Is payroll data secure? Reputable payroll providers use bank-level encryption, maintain SOC 2 compliance, and follow strict data protection protocols. They're often more secure than handling payroll in-house, as they invest heavily in cybersecurity infrastructure and undergo regular security audits. What are the best payroll services for small businesses? The best small business payroll services offer comprehensive payroll services with automated tax calculations and transparent pricing. Rippling, OnPay, Gusto are top choices for small business payroll processing that simplify payroll management and handle payroll expenses effectively. How does payroll software work? Payroll software automates the calculation and processing of employee wages, tax withholdings, deductions, and direct deposits. It also handles payroll tax filing with federal, state, and local agencies, generates pay stubs, and maintains records for compliance purposes. Most platforms include employee self-service portals and integrate with accounting, HR, and time-tracking systems to reduce manual data entry. Can payroll software handle both employees and contractors? Most payroll software can handle both employees and contractors, but the features differ. Employees require tax withholding, benefits deductions, and W-2 generation. Contractors are paid gross without withholdings, and most platforms generate 1099s at year-end. Some providers also support international contractor payments across multiple currencies, which is useful for remote or globally distributed teams. Can I switch payroll providers without losing historical data? Yes. Switching payroll providers is common, and most modern platforms support data migration from prior systems. You'll typically need to export historical payroll records, YTD figures, and employee data from your current provider before importing into the new one. The cleanest time to switch is at the start of a new calendar year or quarter, though mid-year transitions are possible with careful YTD reconciliation. Most providers offer onboarding support to help with the migration. title: Constellium to Source Local Renewable Energy for its German Facilities
summary: PARIS, July 15, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Constellium SE (NYSE: CSTM) today announced that its extrusion and automotive structures plants in Gottmadingen...
body_text: PARIS, July 15, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Constellium SE (NYSE: CSTM) today announced that its extrusion and automotive structures plants in Gottmadingen and Singen , Germany, will source locally produced solar electricity under a long-term Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) with the community of Gottmadingen. Under the agreement, Constellium will receive the full electricity output of the Katzental solar park over a 10-year period, produced locally in the immediate vicinity of the Gottmadingen and Singen plants. The electricity will be used exclusively by Constellium’s Gottmadingen and Singen extrusion and automotive structures plants, covering over 25% of the plants’ combined total needs. The agreement is expected to avoid approximately 3,500 metric tons of CO₂ emissions per year1. “This initiative is an important step in our efforts to reduce our environmental footprint, strengthen the energy resilience of our operations, and support our long-term competitiveness in Germany,” said Stéphane Corre, President of Constellium’s Automotive Structures and Industry business unit. “By sourcing renewable electricity produced directly in the region, we are strengthening our offering of low-carbon solutions to our customers.” Deliveries from Katzental solar park to Constellium are planned from spring 2027, following the installation of the electrical infrastructure required for direct supply to Constellium. Constellium’s Gottmadingen and Singen operations are part of the company’s extrusions business and supply advanced aluminum solutions to customers across key markets, including the automotive industry. The solutions are used in applications such as crash management systems, battery applications for electric vehicles and automotive structural components. About Constellium Constellium (NYSE: CSTM) is a global sector leader that develops innovative, value-added aluminum products for a broad scope of markets and applications, including aerospace, packaging and automotive. Constellium generated $8.4 billion of revenue in 2025. www.constellium.com 1 Estimated avoided emissions calculated using market-based reporting approach for electricity in Germany: 294 gCO₂/kWh. title: The benefits of banking close to home | Columbus | Northwest Bank
summary: Did you know that banking locally offers many of the same advantages? If you’re thinking about banking locally, here’s what to consider and how a new financial center in Columbus could give you another option close to home.
body_text: Education | July 27, 2026 The Benefits of Banking Close to Home: Local accounts for local customers Keeping your bank close to home benefits you and your community Key takeaways: If you love supporting local businesses, consider banking locally as well. Local banking is convenient — our expansion allows customers to visit financial centers in New Albany, Gahanna and Westerville as well as Columbus proper — and offers service with a friendly, community-minded feel. A local bank also offers solutions designed for households and businesses across the Columbus area, so you get personalized service. You know all about the benefits of shopping locally. But did you know that banking locally offers many of the same advantages? “Like shopping with local small businesses, banking locally means your money stays in the community, where it can help build thriving neighborhood s, ” says Anthony Hapney, m anager of our New Albany Financial Center , the first of four new locations opening across the Columbus area . “But more than that, choosing a neighborhood bank can significantly impact the experience you have, just like when you choose a local business.” If you’re thinking about banking locally, here’s what to consider and how a new financial center in Columbus could give you another option close to home. How is a local bank different from a national bank? As the name suggests, national banks have a nationwide , or even an international, footprint. That can offer some advantages: For example, you’re likely to find a bank ATM from virtually anywhere in the country. Pro tip: We're part of the AllPoint ATM network , a network of more than 55,000 ATMs located around the world. That means you can find an ATM to withdraw money without surcharges, even if you’re far from home. But a national presence can also create a “big bank” atmosphere. Because national banks serve customers across many markets, the experience can feel less connected to the needs of a specific community. With such a broad footprint, it can be harder to shape the experience around what matters most in a specific market. Local banks take a different approach. They typically operate locations within specific areas — anywhere from a handful of states to a network of local communities — which means they’re deeply rooted in the communities they serve. “Local banking is all about creating a welcoming , people-first atmosphere and serving as a cornerstone of the neighborhood,” says Hapney. “That kind of relationship shows up in small but important ways, from how you’re greeted when you walk in to how conversations and recommendations are handled.” Did you know? Our expansion in the Columbus region starts with four new financial centers: New Albany, Gahanna, Westerville and Columbus . We're excited to offer tailored support to families across the area. Find your local financial center. How does having a local banker actually impact your banking experience? Beyond providing a friendly community atmosphere, keeping your money close to home can lead to a better banking experience, too. Here’s why: Products, services and solutions tailored to you One benefit of local banking is working with a bank that can better reflect the needs of the people and businesses in the community it serves. “As local bankers, we can have more relevant conversations because we understand the market people are living and working in," says Hapney. "That matters whether someone is buying a home, opening an account or running a business here in Columbus.” Get generation-specific insights: Learn about smart money habits for Gen Z , as well as financial wellness for Millennials. Convenient service that fits your daily life Beyond helping you find solutions personalized to your needs, a local bank makes it convenient for you to manage your financial health. One clear benefit: Your local bank is right in your neighborhood. So it’s easy to stop in when you're shopping nearby or coming home from a family adventure at the Blendon Woods Metro Park. We're opening financial centers in New Albany, Gahanna, Westerville and North High Street . Click here to learn more about our expansion across the Columbus area. Local banks may also offer faster service, particularly when it comes to loans, mortgages and other forms of credit. “At a local bank, the person processing your application might be just down the hall, which makes it easier for your banker to keep you in the loop throughout the process,” says Hapney. “At a national bank, that person could be hours away, which can make the application process feel less transparent — and, for some, much more intimidating.” Pro tip: In addition to a convenient in- person experience, our online and mobile banking tools make it easy to manage your finances, from building budgets to setting savings goals . A bank that just gets it Putting down deep roots in the community offers another significant advantage: The ability to hit the ground running when you come in for financial advice. “We’re on top of what’s happening in the community and trends impacting business owners and households,” says Hapney. “And not just because we’re helping other local customers going through similar experiences. We have a personal stake in the community because we live here too. We’re seeing the same challenges as you, and we’re looking for opportunities to help.” How we can help you reach your goals Whether you’re buying a first home, planning for retirement or figuring out what makes sense for your next move, it helps to have someone who can walk through the options with you. Sometimes, that involves helping you open an account or apply for a loan. But most of the time, it’s about answering questions and helping you understand your financial options so you can make informed decisions about your money. How can we help? Trusted insights and advice: Our team is here to answer any questions you might have about money, from how to build (and use) an emergency fund to how to manage cash flow for your small business . Checking and savings accounts that fit how you manage your money: No matter what your goals are or how you prefer to manage your money, we’ll help you find the right account for you . Lending options for personal and business needs: Whether you’re looking for a mortgage, a small business loan or another form of credit, we can help you understand what may fit. Most of all, we want to be a familiar, trusted presence in the neighborhood — a place where people can get answers, talk through options and build real relationships over time. Our first Columbus financial center opens on July 13 in New Albany at 5746 N Hamilton Road . Stop by to meet the team, ask questions and learn more about the accounts, services and support available to you. Did you know? We're offering high-yield Performance Savings accounts specifically for consumers in Ohio — and you can open your account now. Learn more about the account and how to get started banking with us. title: Gemini Predicted: CLARITY Act Odds Increase After White House Agrees to Ethics Provision, Crypto Continues Rally, and LA Rams Emerge as Super Bowl Favorite
summary: The price of bitcoin dipped pushed back above $66,000 on Tuesday after the White House reportedly agreed to an ethics provision in the Clarity Act.
body_text: Welcome to Gemini Predicted, a weekly newsletter where markets tell us the news. Gemini Predicted is built around a simple premise: prediction markets are one of the most honest signals we have about what's actually happening in the world. That's why we publish this weekly newsletter to keep you informed. Predictions Market Pulse (Politics) Clarity Act odds rise: The odds of Congress passing the CLARITY Act before the end of the year jumped to 57% on Tuesday morning after the White House reportedly agreed to an ethics provision that had held up negotiations. While the full text of the new bill has not been released, lawmakers now could potentially bring the bill to the Senate floor for a vote by the end of the week, with bitcoin rallying past $66,000 Tuesday morning on hopes of a deal. Lawmakers have until the August recess to push the legislation to a floor vote, and it will need to pass the House of Representatives with a simple majority vote before President Donald Trump can sign it into law. (Crypto) Strong ETF inflows bolster ether rally: The price of ethereum jumped past $1,900 on Monday and continued to rally Tuesday, continuing its move higher as ethereum spot ETFs recorded $105 million in net inflows. The price of ethereum has now increased more than 11% over the past month, surpassing bitcoin’s roughly 3.5% gain as institutional investors showed some renewed interest in altcoins. As of Tuesday afternoon, Gemini Predictions traders had priced in a 29% chance the price of ether would surpass $2,000 by the end of the month. (Sports) Traders await Alcaraz update ahead of US Open: With the US Open a little more than a month away, Jannik Sinner has emerged as the favorite to win the tournament, at 55%, followed by Carlos Alcaraz at 31%, according to Gemini Predictions. But Alcaraz is still recovering from a right wrist injury he suffered in April, forcing him to miss the French Open and Wimbledon. The World No. 3 has yet to commit to playing in the US Open and was spotted at the World Cup final on Sunday sporting a bandage on his right wrist. Contract Spotlight Who will win the Ballon d’Or this year? When Spain defeated Argentina 1-0 in the World Cup final over the weekend, it marked the culmination of a 39-day soccer extravaganza that grabbed the sporting world’s attention. But there’s a major individual award that officials have yet to announce: the Ballon d’Or. The Ballon d’Or is given out annually to the best soccer player in the world across international and club play, with an international collection of soccer journalists voting on the prize. This year’s award will be announced on October 26 in London. With a little more than three months before the announcement, traders have tabbed England’s Harry Kane to win the prize (45%), followed by Spain’s Lamine Yamal (12%), and France’s Kylian Mbappé (11%). Kane is coming off a dominant season at Bayern Munich in the Bundesliga league, with 36 goals in 31 games, before leading England to the World Cup semifinals. Yamal had 16 goals and 11 assists in 28 games for FC Barcelona in Spain’s La Liga, and Mbappé was a dominant presence for Real Madrid before scoring 10 goals in the World Cup. On the Radar 2027 Pro Football Champion With the World Cup over, it is never too early to turn attention to football. And traders have done just that, with the 2027 Pro Football Champion contract pulling in more than $21,000 in volume.
